supports.excerpt:
Additional parts of the standard library are shipped as separate libraries. These include:

- `scala.reflect` - Scala's reflection API (scala-reflect.jar)
- `scala.xml` - XML parsing, manipulation, and serialization (scala-xml.jar)
- `scala.collection.parallel` - Parallel collections (scala-parallel-collections.jar)
- `scala.util.parsing` - Parser combinators (scala-parser-combinators.jar)
- `scala.swing` - A convenient wrapper around Java's GUI framework called Swing (scala-swing.jar)

####  Automatic imports
Identifiers in the scala package and the `scala.Predef` object are always in scope by default.

skill_drafts.name: Scala Standard Library Module Resolution
skill_drafts.description: Reference guide for optional Scala standard library modules and their corresponding JAR artifacts. Use when configuring Scala project dependencies or verifying available standard library components.
skill_drafts.objective: Provide lookup mapping between Scala optional modules and their JAR artifacts
constraints: Reference only; does not execute module loading
Modules listed are optional and must be explicitly included
JAR artifacts must be available in build repository or local classpath
output_contract: Documented mapping of optional Scala modules to their JAR files, enabling caller to add required artifacts to build configuration or classpath

metadata.prompt: Consult this reference to identify which optional Scala standard library modules are needed for your project and map them to their JAR artifact names. Each module is shipped separately and must be explicitly added to your build configuration or classpath.

skill_drafts.name: Scala Automatic Scope Injection
skill_drafts.description: Reference for automatic availability of identifiers from scala package and scala.Predef in Scala code without explicit import statements. Use when debugging unresolved identifier errors or understanding default namespace behavior.
skill_drafts.objective: Reference automatic import behavior for core Scala identifiers
applicable_signals: Question about implicit imports in Scala
Need to document default namespace availability
contraindications: Handling package shadowing or name conflicts
Configuring custom predef or alternative standard library
triggers: Troubleshooting unresolved identifier errors, understanding implicit imports, or documenting Scala namespace defaults
constraints: Applies only to scala.* and scala.Predef identifiers
Does not cover separately shipped libraries (scala.reflect, scala.xml, scala.swing, etc.)
Automatic scope is standard Scala behavior; custom configurations may override
cautions: Separately shipped libraries (scala-reflect.jar, scala-xml.jar, scala-parallel-collections.jar, scala-parser-combinators.jar, scala-swing.jar) require explicit dependency and import declarations
Name shadowing or local redefinition can override automatic scope
output_contract: Confirmation that scala.* and scala.Predef identifiers are available without explicit import statement; clarity on which identifiers are automatically in scope versus which require explicit dependency or import

metadata.prompt: Scala automatically makes all identifiers in the scala package and scala.Predef object available in scope by default. This means you can use core Scala types, functions, and utilities without writing explicit import statements. When troubleshooting identifier resolution errors, check whether the identifier belongs to scala.* or scala.Predef before adding imports.
